newsitem.title: USA: N.H. militia member guilty of $100,000 Army heist.
newsitem.headline: N.H. militia member guilty of $100,000 Army heist.

text.p: A New Hampshire man pleaded guilty Monday to federal charges that he helped steal $100,000 in military aviation equipment from Fort Devens Army base 18 months ago.

Fitzhugh MacCrae, 51, also known as Kenneth Nepil, of Nashua and a member of the Hillsborough County Dragoons militia group, admitted to three counts of conspiring to steal government property, theft of government property and lying to the FBI, the U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Donald Stern said.
The thefts involved stealing $100,000 worth of aviation night vision devices and other military equipment from Fort Devens in Massachusetts and then delivering the goods to MacCrae's home.
MacCrae told his co-conspirators, Brian Chabot and Eldon Brooks, that he would make arrangements to distribute the equipment to militia members and interested buyers, Stern said in a statement.
Brooks previously pleaded uilty to conspiracy and theft of government property. Similar charges are pending against Chabot, prosecutors said.

U.S. District Judge Robert Keeton set a May 14 date for MacCrae's sentencing. He faces up to five years in prison on the conspiracy charge and making false statements to the FBI and 10 years on the theft charge. He also faces fines of up to $250,000 on each count.
